title: Make the reuse registry an approval-time research input instead of an implementation/policy file

scope.subject: Reuse-gate registry lifecycle and approval semantics

research_summary: The v2 gate correctly hash-locks registry.json into each approval, but currently also classifies the registry as a protected policy implementation file. That makes the documented workflow impossible: research is supposed to update the persistent registry before reuse:approve, while approval refuses dirty protected files. Reuse the catalog/decision-record model where catalog evidence is an input to a decision, not executable policy. Keep the registry SHA-256 freeze after approval, while only the gate script, policy instructions, README and hooks remain policy files.

sources.finding: Backstage treats catalog entities as maintained descriptive metadata about systems/components; the catalog is data consumed by workflows rather than the policy engine itself.

Architecture decision records use evidence/context as inputs to a decision and preserve the decision separately, supporting the distinction between mutable research evidence before approval and frozen decision state afterward.

Policy-as-code systems distinguish policy rules from the structured data/configuration being evaluated, supporting keeping enforcement logic protected while allowing evidence inputs to be prepared before evaluation.
Git hooks remain the existing commit-time enforcement surface and do not require research metadata itself to be treated as hook policy code.

search_ladder.conclusion: A software catalog cleanly separates catalog data from executable governance, but deploying Backstage remains disproportionate.
OPA/Conftest makes the policy/data separation explicit but still adds an unnecessary policy runtime for this repository.
Keep the local Node decision gate and make registry data a frozen decision input rather than policy implementation.
Keep Git/npm enforcement unchanged; only correct how registry.json participates in pre-approval dirtiness checks.

coverage_matrix.capability: registry can be updated during research before approval
coverage_matrix.decision: All viable models separate evidence/catalog data from policy code; implement that separation in the lightweight Node gate.

coverage_matrix.capability: registry becomes immutable for an approved implementation task
coverage_matrix.decision: Retain the existing registry SHA-256 in approval.json; any post-approval mutation continues to invalidate the token.

coverage_matrix.capability: policy files cannot be changed by ordinary tasks
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep script/AGENTS/README/hooks under architecture policy_change protection while removing only registry.json from policy classification.

candidates.name: Adopt Backstage catalog/policy separation wholesale
candidates.reason: Its conceptual catalog/data separation is correct, but operating Backstage for one repository remains unnecessary.

candidates.name: Move registry validation into OPA/Conftest data + policy
candidates.reason: It solves the lifecycle cleanly but still adds a separate binary/Rego toolchain for a three-line classification correction.

candidates.name: Keep Node gate; classify registry as research input and hash-lock it after approval
candidates.license: Project code informed by ADR/catalog patterns
candidates.reason: Smallest change, preserves all current enforcement, and resolves the workflow contradiction without weakening post-approval integrity.

candidates.name: Retain Git/npm enforcement surfaces
candidates.reason: No change needed; commit/build enforcement continues to consume the corrected approval semantics.

decision.rationale: Correct only the registry lifecycle classification: registry.json is mutable research evidence before approval and is frozen by SHA-256 after approval; executable gate policy remains protected. This removes a real workflow deadlock without weakening enforcement or adding a governance platform.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Backstage provides a richer catalog platform, but its service footprint is far larger than the single lifecycle bug being fixed; we retain its data-versus-policy separation concept only.
OPA cleanly separates policy and input data, but introducing a second policy language and runtime has lower global value than fixing the existing Node gate directly.

decision.fallback: If registry rules later require cross-repository policy, migrate the same JSON registry and decision schema to OPA/Conftest or Backstage.
